title: Terraform state management
subtitle: Practise S3 locking, handle drift and rename resources without replacing them.

delta.before: S3 locking commonly paired the state bucket with DynamoDB.
delta.after: Try native S3 locks, move state and use moved blocks to keep existing resource IDs.

exercises.title: Lock Contention Lab
exercises.description: Start two local runs and see how a lock keeps them from writing state together.

cost.assumptions: Short-lived resources, no compute, standard parameters, no uploads; gross usage before account credits.

checkpoints.prompt: Moving local state to an S3 backend, which settings/workflow provide native locking and carry the snapshot?

choices.a: use_lockfile=true with init -migrate-state and the intended backend configuration
choices.b: encrypt=true alone; every workspace state merges automatically

rationale.a: Locking is explicit; migration transfers the local snapshot into the selected remote backend.
rationale.b: Encryption is not locking, and state boundaries do not merge automatically.

checkpoints.prompt: Does refresh-only apply restore a console change to the HCL setting?

rationale.a: It updates observations in state rather than changing the remote setting.
rationale.b: A normal plan/apply is needed to reconcile the desired setting.

checkpoints.prompt: What does removed with destroy=false do to the live resource?

choices.a: Leaves it live while removing Terraform ownership

rationale.a: Track it for explicit cleanup in this course.
